fork:bitsat-2022:1.explanation: Most primary amino acids produce a purple ninhydrin product. Proline has a secondary amino group built into a ring, so its ninhydrin reaction instead gives a yellow product. That distinguishes proline on the chromatogram.

fork:bitsat-2022:2.explanation: Heating helps liquid molecules move past one another, reducing liquid viscosity. In a dilute gas, faster molecules transport momentum more readily between adjacent moving layers; its viscosity increases. The two trends correspond to C.

fork:bitsat-2022:3.explanation: Down group 2, increasing cation size reduces polarization of the carbonate ion and makes decomposition of the carbonate less favourable. Among Be, Mg, Ca and Ba carbonates, BaCO₃ therefore has the greatest thermal stability.

fork:bitsat-2022:4.explanation: One phenylhydrazine molecule initially forms a hydrazone with the carbonyl. A second oxidizes the neighbouring alcohol to a carbonyl, and a third condenses at that new carbonyl. Thus three molecules are consumed even though the osazone contains two hydrazone groups.

fork:bitsat-2022:5.explanation: Nylon-6,6 is a polyamide formed by condensation of a six-carbon diamine with a six-carbon dicarboxylic acid. Hexamethylenediamine and adipic acid supply those two units and form amide linkages.

fork:bitsat-2022:6.explanation: Ortho and para hydrogen differ in the relative nuclear spins of their two protons, so their allowed rotational states and some physical properties differ. Both have the same H₂ bonding and the same usual chemical reactions.

fork:bitsat-2022:7.explanation: In [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Br the free counterion is Br⁻, which forms pale-yellow AgBr with silver nitrate. Exchanging coordinated sulfate and outer bromide gives the ionization isomer [Co(NH₃)₅Br]SO₄. Its free SO₄²⁻ forms white BaSO₄ with barium chloride. Hence all three statements apply.

fork:bitsat-2022:8.explanation: Benzotrichloride is C₆H₅CCl₃. Replacing all three benzylic hydrogens of a methyl side chain with chlorine identifies X as toluene. Hydrolysis of the trichloromethyl group converts it to –COOH, so Y is benzoic acid.

fork:bitsat-2022:9.explanation: The inert-pair effect increases down group 14 and makes Pb(II) relatively stable. Pb(IV) tends to accept electrons to reach +2, while Ge(II) tends to lose electrons to reach the more stable Ge(IV). The opposite redox behaviour follows from this change in oxidation-state stability.

fork:bitsat-2022:10.explanation: In an antifluorite lattice the anions form a face-centred cubic array and the cations fill all the tetrahedral holes. There are two such holes per anion, requiring an M₂X composition. Sodium oxide, Na₂O, adopts this arrangement.

fork:bitsat-2022:11.explanation: Pyrophosphoric acid is formed by condensing two H₃PO₄ molecules with loss of water. The resulting P–O–P bridge leaves two OH groups on each phosphorus atom. Across the molecule there are four P–OH bonds.

fork:bitsat-2022:12.explanation: The equilibrium relation ln K = ΔS°/R − ΔH°/(RT) has a temperature-independent intercept ΔS°/R. Matching the constant term 4.0 gives ΔS° = 4R.

fork:bitsat-2022:13.explanation: Adiabatic conditions give q = 0. In free expansion against vacuum the external pressure is zero, so the work is also zero. The first law gives ΔU = 0, and the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature. Thus ΔT = 0.

fork:bitsat-2022:14.explanation: The straight rising line is consistent with the excluded-volume-only model, which gives Z = 1 + bp/(RT). With b = 0 and a nonzero attraction parameter, the van der Waals equation instead gives Z = 1−a/(RTVₘ); Vₘ itself varies with pressure. A straight fall in Z at every pressure does not follow, making B the incorrect claim.

fork:bitsat-2022:15.explanation: In the nonrelativistic one-electron Coulomb model, hydrogen's bound-state energy depends on the principal quantum number n alone. The 3s, 3p and 3d orbitals all have n = 3 and are therefore degenerate in this model.

fork:bitsat-2022:16.explanation: CH₄, NF₃, NH₄⁺ and H₂O each have four electron domains at the central atom. In the usual valence-bond model this gives sp³ hybridization for all four. Lone-pair counts and bond angles differ.

fork:bitsat-2022:17.explanation: AgBr is about 79.9/(107.9+79.9) = 42.5% bromine by mass. Thus 0.12 g of AgBr contains approximately 0.051 g of bromine. Relative to the 0.20 g sample this is about 25.5%, nearest 25%.

fork:bitsat-2022:18.explanation: The diamond moves from left to bottom to right of the central object, so it must next lie above it. At the same time the centre alternates between a partitioned circle and a divided semicircle, and the triangle alternates filled and open. Only A has the diamond above an unshaded semicircle and an open triangle on its right.

fork:bitsat-2022:19.explanation: The second and third views show the same adjacent faces 1 and 2 in reversed order on the visible sides. The two faces that complete those corner views must lie on opposite sides of that common edge. Those faces are 6 and 3, so 3 is opposite 6.

fork:bitsat-2022:20.explanation: Trace the template without rotating it. In B the top ledge, the long return down the right, the short bottom ledge pointing left and the vertical stroke extending below that ledge can all be followed on existing lines. Extra grid lines may be ignored when testing an embedded figure.

fork:bitsat-2022:21.explanation: Split the drawing into its left, centre and right vertical strips. The left strip contains eight triangles in its fully crossed upper cell, four in the lower cell, and one tall triangle spanning both cells. Counting by complete straight edges gives 13 on the left. The right strip is its half-turn counterpart, also giving 13. In the middle the common lower apex gives three triangles between the top endpoints and two more against the vertical sides. No triangle crosses a strip boundary. The total is 13+5+13 = 31.

fork:bitsat-2022:22.explanation: The reported total is 50×64 = 3200. Removing the two erroneous scores and adding their true values gives 3200−38−42+83+24 = 3227. Dividing by 50 gives the corrected mean of 64.54.

fork:bitsat-2022:23.explanation: A mirror on the right reverses left and right while keeping vertical positions. The filled dot moves left of the rectangle, the plus moves right, and the little diamond moves to its lower-left corner. The curved corner marks switch sides as well. These features all appear in A.

fork:bitsat-2022:24.explanation: Fix B at the top and list seats clockwise, which is the leftward direction for people facing in. A must take seat 4 if B is seat 0. Placing E two clockwise from C and away from both neighbours of B forces C into seat 1 and E into seat 3. Therefore A in seat 4 sits immediately left of E, regardless of the remaining D/F order.

fork:bitsat-2022:25.explanation: The comparisons give E > B > C in price, and C > A > D. Combining them gives E, B, C, A, D from most to least costly. B bought the second most expensive car.

fork:bitsat-2022:26.explanation: The bottom-left panel has a diagonal from its lower left to the upper right, with a short line from the diagonal down to its lower right. Reflecting that panel in the central vertical line gives the missing lower-right panel. It must have a descending diagonal and a short line from its midpoint to the lower-left corner, as in B.

fork:bitsat-2022:27.explanation: Compare the first row: two dots in the first cell become four in the second. Applying the same doubling rule to the three dots in the lower-left cell gives six dots. Only D has six.

fork:bitsat-2022:28.explanation: The given pieces include one small four-right-angle piece, two sloping four-sided pieces and one triangle. In B the upper-right region takes the small rectangular piece, the lower-left region takes the triangle, and the two remaining regions accept the sloping pieces. The other partitions split the pieces into incompatible shapes or numbers of regions.

fork:bitsat-2022:29.explanation: The relationship is tool to function. A needle is used to sew, and a microscope is used to magnify an image. Laboratory, lens and science describe a setting, a part or a field instead of that function.

fork:bitsat-2022:30.explanation: The pairs follow n → (n+3)², since (14+3)² = 289 and (17+3)² = 400. With n = 21 the result is 24² = 576.

fork:bitsat-2022:31.explanation: The sum of the two roots is −1/2, so the other root is −1/2−α. Using 4α² = 1−2α gives 4α³−3α = −2α−2α² = −α−1/2. This identifies C.

fork:bitsat-2022:32.explanation: The intersection contains integers divisible by both 4 and 6. Their least common multiple is 12, from 4 = 2² and 6 = 2×3. The common multiples are exactly the multiples of 12.

fork:bitsat-2022:34.explanation: For small t, 1−cos t is t²/2 to leading order. Here t = 1−cos x is itself x²/2 to leading order. The numerator therefore behaves as (x²/2)²/2 = x⁴/8, yielding 1/8.

fork:bitsat-2022:35.explanation: Adding the two ninth powers cancels terms with odd powers of 5√(2x). The surviving binomial indices are 0, 2, 4, 6 and 8, which produce five distinct powers of x.

fork:bitsat-2022:36.explanation: Choose the two positions occupied by the digit 2 in C(7,2) ways. Each of the other five positions may independently hold 1 or 3. With no zero available, every arrangement is seven digits long. The total is C(7,2) × 2⁵.

fork:bitsat-2022:37.explanation: Subtracting the second equation from the first gives x+y+3z = 6. For λ = 3 the third equation has the identical left side but sets it equal to 4. This contradiction makes the system inconsistent.

fork:bitsat-2022:38.explanation: Because AB = I, A times the displayed 10B must equal 10I. Its (1,3) entry is the dot product of (1,−1,1) with (2,α,3), or 5−α. This off-diagonal entry must vanish, giving α=5.

fork:bitsat-2022:41.explanation: The quotient derivative gives d(y/tan x)/dx = (y′tan x−y sec²x)/tan²x = sin x/tan²x. Rewrite this as csc x−sin x. Its antiderivative is ln abs(csc x−cot x)+cos x+C. Multiply by tan x to obtain A.

fork:bitsat-2022:42.explanation: The parabola is y² = 4a(x−a²), the standard parabola shifted right by a². In shifted coordinates X = x−a², its slope-m tangent is y=mX+a/m. Returning to x gives the constant term c = a/m−ma².

fork:bitsat-2022:43.explanation: Write the point as (2t²,4t) on y²=8x. The tangent slope is 1/t, hence the normal slope is −t. Taking the normal’s inclination as +60° relative to the horizontal y=8 gives t=−√3. The point is (6,−4√3), which satisfies 2x−y−12−4√3=0.

fork:bitsat-2022:44.explanation: Let u=[(x−1)/(x+2)]¹ᐟ⁴. Differentiating gives du/dx = (3/4)(x−1)⁻³ᐟ⁴(x+2)⁻⁵ᐟ⁴ on x>1. Thus the listed antiderivative there is (4/3)u+C. The expression also differentiates correctly on the real branch x<−2 when the original fourth root is taken positive.

fork:bitsat-2022:45.explanation: Write the parabola as x=(y−2)²+1. At y=3 its derivative dx/dy is 2, giving the tangent x=2y−4. Between y=0 and y=3 the horizontal distance from tangent to parabola is (y−3)². Its integral over that interval is 9 square units.

fork:bitsat-2022:46.explanation: The half-sum (u+v)/2 is perpendicular to the cross product, so their squared lengths add to 1 by the given norm. For two unit vectors the parallelogram identity gives magnitude((u+v)/2)² + magnitude((u−v)/2)² = 1. Subtracting the common first term establishes the claimed equality of lengths in D.

fork:bitsat-2022:47.explanation: The per-roll probabilities of odd and even are 3/4 and 1/4. A sum is even if both rolls are odd or both are even. For independent rolls this gives (3/4)²+(1/4)² = 10/16 = 5/8.

fork:bitsat-2022:48.explanation: The product of the three cosines is cos(3θ)/4. The equation reduces to cos(3θ)=1, so θ=2kπ/3 for k=0 through 9 on the closed interval. Their sum is (2π/3)(0+1+⋯+9) = 30π.

fork:bitsat-2022:49.explanation: Let t=16^(sin²θ), so the other term is 16/t. The equation t+16/t=10 has roots 2 and 8. Because θ is below π/4, t<4 and t=2, giving sin²θ=1/4 and α=30°. The height-to-shadow ratio is √3, so the sun's altitude is 60° = 2α.

fork:bitsat-2022:50.explanation: The six letters with three indistinguishable As have 6!/3! = 120 arrangements. If V and N are adjacent, combine them into a block with two internal orders. This gives 2×5!/3! = 40 prohibited arrangements, leaving 80.

fork:bitsat-2022:51.explanation: Taking the common parameter along the line gives direction vector (2b/3,−1,a). Parallelism to the plane means its dot product with (3,1,2) is zero. Thus 2b−1+2a = 0 and 3a+3b = 3/2.

fork:bitsat-2022:52.explanation: Writing t=tan θ, the inverse of the second matrix is 1/(1+t²) times the first. Multiplying therefore gives diagonal entries (1−t²)/(1+t²) and lower-left entry 2t/(1+t²). These are cos 2θ and sin 2θ, respectively.

fork:bitsat-2022:53.explanation: Expand ln(1+x)/x = 1−x/2+x²/3+O(x³). Exponentiating yields (1+x)^(1/x) = e[1−x/2+(1/3+1/8)x²+O(x³)]. After cancellation of the constant and linear terms, division by x² gives 11e/24.

fork:bitsat-2022:54.explanation: Let P=(a,b) be the point from which the two tangents are drawn. Its chord of contact is ax+by=9. The chord midpoint is the foot of the perpendicular from the origin, so if M=(x,y), then (a,b)=9(x,y)/(x²+y²). Substitution into 4a−5b=20 yields 20(x²+y²)−36x+45y=0, with only points from real tangents realized.

fork:bitsat-2022:55.explanation: With s=√(1+x²), rationalize x²/(1+s)=s−1. The integrand reduces to 1/√(1+x²)−1/(1+x²). Integrating from 0 to 1 gives ln(1+√2)−arctan 1 = ln(1+√2)−π/4.

fork:bitsat-2022:56.explanation: The five numbers sum to 20, so the two missing ones satisfy a+b=11. Their total sum of squares is 5(5.2+4²)=106. Subtracting 1²+2²+6² gives a²+b²=65. Thus 2ab=121−65=56 and the numbers with sum 11 and product 28 are 4 and 7.

fork:bitsat-2022:57.explanation: Let x be term 11, the shared end of the arithmetic sequence and start of the geometric one. The AP midpoint is term 6, five common differences earlier, giving x−10. The GP midpoint is term 16, giving 2⁵x. Equating them gives x=−10/31.

fork:bitsat-2022:58.explanation: Let a=π/8. The argument of 1+sin a+i cos a is π/4−a/2, since its imaginary-to-real ratio is cos a/(1+sin a). Division by its conjugate doubles that argument to 3π/8. A power is purely imaginary when 3nπ/8 equals π/2 modulo π. The smallest positive n is 4.

fork:bitsat-2022:59.explanation: Across the 6 m horizontal separation, the window is 6tan60° = 6√3 m above the base of the first house. The line of sight from the window to the top is perpendicular to that to the base, placing it at 30° above horizontal. Its additional rise is 6tan30° = 2√3 m. The total height is 8√3 m.

fork:bitsat-2022:60.explanation: After 49 min the volume is (4500−72×49)π = 972π m³. Using 4πr³/3 gives r=9 m. Differentiate with respect to time: dr/dt = (−72π)/(4π×9²) = −2/9 m/min, so the rate of decrease is 2/9.

fork:bitsat-2022:61.explanation: The lower curve changes expression at π/4. From 0 to π/4 the difference is 2sin x; from π/4 to π/2 it is 2cos x. Their integrals sum to 4−2√2, equal to 2√2(√2−1).

fork:bitsat-2022:62.explanation: Since α,β,γ are in arithmetic progression, (α+γ)/2 = β. The sine difference factors as 2cos β sin((α−γ)/2). The denominator likewise equals 2sin β sin((α−γ)/2). Dividing at points where the ratio is defined leaves cot β.

fork:bitsat-2022:65.explanation: For two bodies moving in the sound direction at 34 and 17 m/s, a 600 Hz signal sent by the faster trailing body reaches the slower reflector at frequency 600(1500−17)/(1500−34). On the return path the receiver moves toward the reflected sound, giving a second factor (1500+34)/(1500+17). Their product is about 613.8 Hz, agreeing with the listed 613.7 Hz to its stated accuracy.

fork:bitsat-2022:66.explanation: Wave speed is √(T/μ), where μ is mass per unit length. With identical materials, doubling the diameter quadruples μ. For A relative to B, the tension ratio is 1/2 and the linear density ratio is 4. Therefore vₐ/vᵦ = √[(1/2)/4] = 1/(2√2).

fork:bitsat-2022:68.explanation: For uniform Earth density the enclosed mass at radius r scales as r³, making the interior field GM(r)/r² proportional to r. At depth d the radius is R−d. Comparing with the surface gives g(d)=g(1−d/R).

fork:bitsat-2022:69.explanation: Square 6+10sin ωt and average over one cycle. The cross term averages to zero, and the sine-squared term averages to 1/2. Thus Iᵣₘₛ = √(36+100/2)=√86 A ≈ 9.27 A.

fork:bitsat-2022:70.explanation: For a uniformly charged, nonconducting solid sphere the internal field increases linearly from zero at the centre. Since dV/dr=−E, the interior potential falls quadratically with an initially horizontal tangent. Outside the sphere it falls as 1/r towards zero. D shows both parts of this dependence.

fork:bitsat-2022:71.explanation: An insulator has a band gap large enough to suppress ordinary thermal promotion into the conduction band. Among 0, 1, 2 and 5 eV, the widest gap, 5 eV, is the representative insulating value. Actual materials have different gaps.

fork:bitsat-2022:73.explanation: The full 0.20 m square has central perpendicular-axis inertia M a²/6 ≈ 0.006667 kg·m². Each round hole removes mass π/16 kg and its centre is √2R from the square’s centre. Its contribution about the central axis is (π/16)[R²/2+2R²] with R=0.05 m. Subtracting all four leaves about 0.00176 kg·m², nearest C.

fork:bitsat-2022:74.explanation: At the highest point the parent has horizontal speed v cos θ and zero vertical speed. To continue on the original trajectory with the same motion, one equal-mass piece retains that velocity. Conservation of momentum requires the other half also to have horizontal velocity v cos θ and no vertical component.

fork:bitsat-2022:76.explanation: The magnetic and electric fields of a plane electromagnetic wave in free space obey E=cB at each point and time. For E=8 V/m this gives B=8/(3×10⁸) T ≈ 2.67×10⁻⁸ T.

fork:bitsat-2022:77.explanation: Y is 9 V higher than X, so conventional current would flow from right to left. Both ideal diodes point from left to right and are reverse-biased in the consistent circuit state. The surviving path from Y to X consists of 6 Ω, 2 Ω and 8 Ω in series, totalling 16 Ω.

fork:bitsat-2022:78.explanation: For one mole, stopping the container and allowing the translational kinetic energy to thermalize adds mv²/2 to the gas internal energy in this idealized insulated system. A monatomic gas has molar Cᵥ=3R/2. Equating (3R/2)ΔT to mv²/2 gives ΔT=mv²/(3R).

fork:bitsat-2022:79.explanation: The initial horizontal and vertical speeds are 3 and 4 m/s. For landing at the launch height and g≈10 m/s², the flight time is 2×4/10 = 0.8 s. Horizontal travel is then 3×0.8 = 2.4 m.

fork:bitsat-2022:80.explanation: The collector current is 0.6 V / 500 Ω = 1.2 mA. The stated α = Iᴄ/Iᴇ gives common-emitter gain β = α/(1−α)=24. Thus Iʙ = 1.2 mA / 24 = 50 µA.

fork:bitsat-2022:81.explanation: About central symmetry axes, the initial solid-sphere inertia is (2/5)×80×15² = 7200 kg·m² and the final disc inertia is (1/2)×80×20² = 16000 kg·m². Over 3600 s the mean increase is (16000−7200)/3600 = 22/9 kg·m²/s.

fork:bitsat-2022:82.explanation: A permanent magnet must resist demagnetization, so the broader hysteresis loop with greater coercivity is preferred. X has that broader loop. The narrower loop of Y indicates easier magnetization reversal, suited to an electromagnet.

fork:bitsat-2022:83.explanation: Use rightward distances as positive. At the convex interface, u=−20 cm, R=+40 cm, n₁=1 and n₂=1.5. The refraction formula n₂/v−n₁/u=(n₂−n₁)/R gives 1.5/v+1/20=0.5/40. Hence v=−40 cm, a virtual image 40 cm to the left.

fork:bitsat-2022:84.explanation: The line through the origin on the V versus 1/T plot implies VT is constant, hence dV/V=−dT/T. For one mole P=RT/V, so P dV=−R dT. The first law gives δQ=(Cᵥ−R)dT. With Cᵥ=5R/2 for a diatomic gas in this model, the process heat capacity is 3R/2.

fork:bitsat-2022:85.explanation: For steady laminar flow in a capillary at fixed pressure head, Poiseuille’s law gives Q proportional to r⁴. Increasing the radius by 25% multiplies Q by 1.25⁴ ≈ 2.441. The increase relative to the old flow is therefore about 144%.

fork:bitsat-2022:86.explanation: With glass thickness t in each path, the relative optical path introduced is (1.7−1.4)t=0.3t. Displacing the old central maximum by six fringes requires a path difference of 6λ. With λ=400 nm, t=6×400/0.3 nm = 8000 nm = 8 µm.

fork:bitsat-2022:87.explanation: The equal semicircular branches carry equal currents around the centre in opposite senses. Their magnetic fields at the centre cancel, giving zero magnetic force there. In addition, a purely axial magnetic field would be parallel to the axial velocity and have zero magnetic cross product.
